_meta.purpose: Maps HoopsHype's internal numeric team ID (their salary page's hidden 'team' column) to our 3-letter team codes. HoopsHype's salary export uses a numeric ID, not an abbreviation - this table decodes it.
_meta.derivedFrom: A manual HoopsHype salary pull (2026-07-12) cross-referenced against data/nba-rosters/2026-27.csv as ground truth: for every raw row whose player name matched exactly one roster row, the roster's team abbreviation was used to vote on that row's numeric code. 30/30 codes resolved with zero conflicting votes, so this table is currently high-confidence and stable.
caveats: HoopsHype identifies a player by name only (no stable player ID), so their export can contain duplicate/stale rows for the same display name (e.g. a leftover pre-trade cap-hold row alongside the real current one). This table decodes the numeric code correctly, but you still need to pick the right row when a name appears more than once - don't just trust the last occurrence.

HoopsHype abbreviates some first names to a single initial (e.g. 'G. Antetokounmpo', 'S. Gilgeous-Alexander') even for stars, which breaks naive name matching against our full-name records - match by surname (+ first-initial to disambiguate) as a fallback, verified against the roster CSV.
Code 5312 decodes to CHA (Charlotte) - not a typo, just an oddly large ID in HoopsHype's own system.
Re-verify this table on the next HoopsHype refresh (majority-vote it again against the roster CSV) rather than assuming team IDs never change on their end.
